concepts.label: Eligible employee
concepts.definition: An employee of a covered employer who meets the 12-month employment, 1,250 hours of service, and worksite employee threshold requirements.
concepts.quote: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who: (1) Has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, and (2) Has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave ( see § 825.801 for special hours of service requirements for airline flight crew employees), and (3) Is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.

unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to special requirements for airline flight crew employees in § 825.801), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) for employees who work outside the U.S.).

concepts.label: 12 months of employment
concepts.definition: The requirement that an employee must have been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.
concepts.quote: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months

unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer are not required to be consecutive months.

concepts.label: Break in service
concepts.definition: An interruption of employment of seven years or more affecting whether prior employment periods count toward the 12-month requirement.
concepts.quote: employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months

claimants.quote: employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted

unit_attributes.scope_text: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, in determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.logic_text: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted

unit_attributes.object: employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more

qualifications.statement: Exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) require employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years to be counted.

unit_attributes.statement: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more are not required to be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.

concepts.label: Countable employment prior to break in service
concepts.definition: Mandatory inclusion of employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years due to USERRA service or a written rehire agreement.
concepts.quote: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where: (i) The employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA), 38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq., covered service obligation...; or (ii) A written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months when there is a break in service of more than seven years, where the break is occasioned by USERRA-covered service or a written agreement exists concerning rehire.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Either (i) the employee's break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, or (ii) a written agreement exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.logic_text: where: (i) The employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA), 38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq., covered service obligation...; or (ii) A written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service (e.g., for purposes of the employee furthering his or her education or for childrearing purposes).

concepts.label: USERRA absence period
concepts.definition: Period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service counted toward the 12 months of employment.
concepts.quote: The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must be also counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer.

concepts.label: Week of employment
concepts.definition: Any week in which an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of the week, including certain paid or unpaid leave periods.
concepts.quote: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.), the week counts as a week of employment.

claimants.quote: the week counts as a week of employment.

qualifications.statement: An employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer.

concepts.label: Intermittent employment conversion standard
concepts.definition: Deeming 52 weeks equal to 12 months for determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.
concepts.quote: For purposes of determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months.

claimants.quote: 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: For purposes of determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.

concepts.label: Employer discretion to consider prior employment
concepts.definition: An employer's ability to count employment preceding a continuous break in service of more than seven years toward the 12-month employment requirement.
concepts.quote: Nothing in this section prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.

concepts.label: Uniform recognition of prior employment
concepts.definition: The requirement that an employer recognizing prior employment after a break in service of more than seven years must do so uniformly for all similarly situated employees.
concepts.quote: if an employer chooses to recognize such prior employment, the employer must do so uniformly, with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

claimants.quote: the employer must do so uniformly, with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.
